tower: The light at Kerrow has gone dark!
I don't know what's wrong, but in this storm we need her lit.
We can't have wreckers out here again.
Get in there now, ring the office, and find out what's happened!
office: There are three ships due tonight.
The tower's gone dark, and on a night like this!
We can't have wreckers out here again.
Ring the tower and get her lit!

open_call: What? Tregarth's not in the tower?
Then he must have left a good while back.
His log should be in the tower. Check the entries and see which ones hold up.
Ring me when you know, or if you get stuck. I'll help if I can.

both: The keeper is not in the tower. Mr Quick thinks he left some time ago. When did he really leave? Ring Mr Quick with the answer, or if you get stuck.
tower: The log should be on the keeper's desk.
office: The barograph and the weather book are on the weather bench. They show what the weather really did.

log.weather: Gale from the west by evening. Heavy sea.

weather_book.3: W, rising to a gale by evening. Sea very rough.
weather_book.4: WSW, strong gale. Rain. Sea high.
weather_book.5: W, gale. Squalls. Sea very high.

docs.glass_card: Compare each noon with the noon before. Up more than 2: rising. Down more than 2: falling. Down more than 8: falling fast. Anything else: steady.

notices.head: The Kerrow Packet
notices.body: New tenants at Carn Du. The Penhale brothers have at last taken the old cottage on the cliff, and were seen carrying in their furniture on Saturday.

notices.head: Warning to mariners
notices.body: Captain Ezra Jago of the Cormorant is barred from Penmor harbour, by order of the magistrates, following two convictions for running contraband.

cast: Their grandfather was hanged for wrecking. People still lower their voices when they pass the cottage.
Wants Kerrow Point fitted with an automatic lamp. “A keeper costs money.” Tends the breakwater light himself.
Rows the paraffin out to the tower. Everyone says he gives short measure.
Twice fined for running French brandy into coves at night. Barred from Penmor harbour, so he never sets foot there.
Thirty-one years on the rock. A widower, with one daughter, long grown and gone.
watch: warm lights, many together, low on Penmor Head
flashes with no rhythm: short and long groups, never the same twice
